title: Mamdani undergoes surgery to repair his Achilles tendon after soccer injury | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

The mayor of America’s largest city got benched on Friday.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani had surgery to repair his Achilles tendon, which he tore earlier this month while playing soccer with a group of reporters.

The friendly game between Mamdani – a rabid fan of the Beautiful Game– and the City Hall press corps was originally intended to be off the record. But Mamdani was forced to kick the details out into the public last week as he hobbled into a news conference with the help of crutches and an orthopedic medical walking boot.

“I scored a goal soon after getting on the pitch, and I forgot that I was 35,” Mamdani said during a November 20 news conference in the rotunda of City Hall. “Soon after, I tore my Achilles.”

The injury, which the mayor attributed to a lack of proper stretching, did not keep him from boasting that his team had defeated the press corps 10-5.

A reporter who participated in the game described the moment and said the mayor had “crumbled on his own.” No members of the opposing team contributed to the injury.

“The surgery was successful, and the Mayor is expected to make a full recovery,” Mamdani’s Press Secretary Joe Calvello said in a statement Friday. “He was discharged from the hospital and is now resting comfortably at Gracie Mansion.”

City Hall has declined to provide the details of which hospital performed the surgery, citing the mayor’s right to patient confidentiality.

“I’m going to be laid out for a couple of days,” Mamdani said during a news conference this week.

Achilles repair is commonly performed under general anesthesia, according to John Hopkins Medicine. The mayor’s spokesperson said that was the case for Mamdani’s procedure, which typically requires an incision on the back of the calf to allow surgeons to stitch the tendon back together.

The timing also means Mamdani will be forced to skip the annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, which was postponed until Saturday because of the weather. Mamdani is not expected to attend any events over the weekend and a return to work is planned for Monday, according to City Hall.

The injury has been a logistical challenge for the mayor so far. He usually keeps a packed schedule with public press events nearly every day. Social media videos show Mamdani has not missed a beat, even if he’s moving slowly and limping along as hearrivesto cultural celebrations, photo opportunities and turkeydistributionsover the past few days.

A mayoral injury is to be taken seriously. New York City’s charter clearly outlines a line of succession should a sitting mayor become unable to perform the job, be absent from the city for more than nine consecutive days or be removed from office.

In this instance, New York City’s charter requires City Hall to put a plan in place while Mamdani is expected to be medically incapacitated.

While Mamdani spent part of the day in the hospital on Friday, a City Hall spokesperson said First Deputy Mayor Dean Fuleihan, a veteran of municipal government who has served on multiple administrations, would be filling in for him followed by Julia Kerson, the deputy mayor for operations.

Mamdani is not the first New York City mayor to face a medical challenge while in office. Former Mayor Bill de Blasio had surgery on his knee in 2020 and underwent a procedure for a hernia in 2015. Eric Adams, Mamdani’s predecessor, was under full anesthesia during a colonoscopy in 2025.

Mamdani, who usually walks at a brisk New York City pace, now travels with a stool, which is set up to provide relief and get him off his feet during news conferences that can drag on. The mayor’s vulnerability was on display this week when reporters asked how he was feeling ahead of the procedure.

“I’m scared,” Mamdani said. “It’s my first surgery.”
